PROJECT DESCRIPTION

Transplants Brewing is a microbrewery with a Type 23 (Small Beer Manufacturer)
Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control (ABC) License at 40242 La Quinta Lane,
Units 101 and 102, that manufactures and sells craft beer. The applicant is proposing to
construct a 150 square foot alcohol service area, a men’s and women’s restroom and a
120 square foot walk-in cooler within the existing building to better serve patrons.
Microbreweries do not have a maximum floor area requirement for the sale, display and
storage of alcohol.

BACKGROUND

CUP  14-023  was  approved  by  the  Planning  Commission  on
December 23, 2014, through RESOLUTION NO. PC-2014-047, to establish the
microbrewery for the manufacturing, consumption, and on- and off-site sales of beer.

CUP 14-023 MM No. 1 was approved by the Planning Commission on May 12, 2016,
through RESOLUTION NO. PC-2016-022. The modification revised the hours of
operation for the tasting room from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 a.m. Monday through Sunday.

CUP 14-023 MM No. 2 was approved by the Planning Commission on June 14, 2018,
through RESOLUTION NO. PC-2018-019. The modification further extended the hours
of operation for the tasting room from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. Monday through Sunday
and increased the tasting area by allowing an expansion into an adjacent unit for
increased seating area for patrons.

The subject application was submitted on April 28, 2021, and after resolution of
completeness items, was deemed complete and scheduled for the July 8, 2021,
Planning Commission meeting.

Special Findings For Alcoholic Beverage Establishments

In addition to the standard CUP findings required in Palmdale Municipal Code
(PMC) Section 17.22.050, the Planning Commission must also find that the proposed use
is consistent with the purpose of PMC Section 17.92.070.  Items that the
Planning Commission may consider in making this finding include Over Intensification,
High Crime Area, Surrounding Area, and Hours of Operation. These factors are detailed
below.

Over Intensification

PMC Section 17.16.010.A provides two methods to determine Over Intensification for
both On-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments and Off-Sale Alcoholic Beverage
Establishments: Population Density Method and Retail Density Method. However,
Transplants Brewery is considered an Other Alcoholic Beverage Establishment, which is
defined in PMC Section 17.16.010A as “Those establishments that are authorized by
State law to sell, serve, or give away alcoholic beverages for consumption on the
premises; and/or sell, serve or give away alcoholic beverages for consumption off the
premises. The definition includes microbreweries (ABC Type 23) license and veteran’s
 Staff Report to the Planning Commission
CUP 14-023 MM No. 3
July 8, 2021
Page 7

clubs (ABC Type 52). Although the definition for over intensification does not include
Other Alcoholic Beverage Establishments, the over intensification analysis is provided
below.

Population Density Method

  Over Intensification of On/Off-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments shall occur
  where the ratio of the resident population to the permitted On/Off-Sale Alcoholic
  Beverage Establishments (as defined by ABC) within the census tract or census
  division exceeds the ratio of population to On/Off-Sale Alcoholic Beverage
  Establishments for the City.

This is a modification of an existing Other Alcoholic Beverage Establishment and
therefore approval will not impact the number of existing Other Alcoholic Beverage
Establishments. As summarized in TABLE 5 and TABLE 6, the Population Density
Method reveals there will be an over intensification of Other Alcoholic Beverage
Establishments in Census Tract 9102.01, because no Other-Sale ABC licenses are
allowed within the tract and two currently exist. It should be noted that due to the small
population within Census Tract 9102.01, the population density method will yield an over
intensification for any just one Other Alcoholic Beverage Establishment within this tract.

Retail Density Method

  Over Intensification of On/Off-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments shall occur
  where the number of On/Off-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within a
  radius of 2,500 feet of any location in question exceeds the average of the numbers
  of On/Off-Sale Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within a radius of 2,500 feet of
  a sample of 20 Other Alcoholic Beverage Establishments drawn at random from
  the City’s commercially zoned areas.

There are four Other Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within the City of Palmdale as
indicated in TABLE 6. Radii of 2,500 feet were drawn around each establishment and
the number of establishments per each radius ranged from one to two establishments
with a total of four (some of the radii overlap resulting in a higher number of
establishments than the Population Density Method). Therefore, by this method, this
industrial area may have one and a half establishments (6/4=1.5) and does experience
Over Intensification of Other Alcoholic Beverage Establishments because there are
two Other Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within the 2,500-foot radius of the project
site, including Transplants Brewing. It should be noted that due to the small number of
Other Alcoholic Beverage Establishments within the City, the retail density method will
yield an over intensification at any site within 2,500 feet of one another site.

High Crime Area

A high crime area is defined by PMC Section 17.16.080, as an area having a crime rate
of 120% or more of the average of the reporting districts within the City. According to the
Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, there are 33 Crime Report Districts (CRD)
within the City of Palmdale, with a total of 8,186 Part I and Part II Crimes reported for the
year 2019. The average number of combined Part I and Part II Crime offenses for the
reporting period, for all 33 districts, was 248 (8,186 Part I and Part II Crimes/ 33 CRD),
and 20% greater than that average will be 298 (252 x 1.20). The project is within
CRD 2619 (FIGURE 4), which had a total of 695 Part I and Part II offenses, according to
data from the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department, Palmdale Station, 2019 Incidents
by Reporting District report. Therefore, the proposed use is within a crime reporting area
that exhibits a crime rate that is 280% [(695 / 248) x 100] of the Citywide average. As
such, the project site is an area that exhibits high crime.

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department provided the most current location and
date information for Part I and Part II crimes reported for 2018. As shown on the
City of Palmdale CRD 2619 map, (FIGURE 4), the crimes are mainly concentrated in the
vicinity of 10th Street West and Rancho Vista Boulevard. Transplants Brewery is located
approximately a mile north of this area.

Calls for Service

The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department provided a summary of service calls and
crime history for the project site between June 14, 2020, to June 15, 2021, and the report
indicates there were two calls for service. One call was for street racing but when the
Deputy arrived on scene, there were no vehicles racing. The second call was for
inappropriate acts in a vehicle. All calls for service have been routine in nature.
The Los Angeles County Sheriff’s Department has not indicated any opposition to the
approval of this modification. In addition, as specified within the draft Conditions of
Approval, if the proposed business generates an increase in the number of calls for
service, the Los Angeles Sheriff’s Department may request a subsequent review of the
CUP by the Planning Commission.

Surrounding Area

There are no sensitive uses such as residential properties, schools, hospitals, sexually
oriented businesses, public parks, or religious assemblies located within 1,000 feet of the
project site. The surrounding area includes other industrial businesses, vacant land, and
the Antelope Valley County Club Golf Course to the south.

Operations

Transplants is a microbrewery that manufactures and sells beer for consumption both on
and off the premise. The major modification is to construct a 150 square foot alcohol
service area, a men’s and women’s restroom and 120 square foot walk-in cooler to better
serve patrons within the existing footprint of the building.

The microbrewery is currently open from 11:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m. Monday through Sunday
and there are no proposed changes to the hours of operation. The hours of operation are
consistent with the hours established by the ABC for the sale of alcoholic beverages which
is between 6:00 a.m. to 2:00 a.m.

ENVIRONMENTAL REVIEW

The proposed project is Categorically Exempt from California Environmental Quality Act
review pursuant to Section 15301, Class 1 of the CEQA Guidelines, which exempts minor
alterations of existing buildings. The proposed modification will alter the existing building
by constructing a new 150 square foot alcohol service area, a men’s and women’s
restroom and a 120 square foot walk-in cooler within an existing tenant space.

SUBJECT:  Conditional Use Permit 17-016

DATE:  July 8, 2021

Staff has received an incident crime report from the Los Angeles County Sheriff’s
Department regarding reported crimes at Pro Club, a bail bond and check cashing facility
located at 1475 East Palmdale Boulevard, Suite C. The report details illegal activity by
the tenant including possession of a firearm with the intent to commit a felony, possession
of narcotics with a firearm, possession of controlled substances for sale, and operating or
minting a drug house. The report further describes patrons using three illegal gambling
machines known as “Tap Tap” machines. The bail bond and check cashing facility to
allow customers an opportunity to process transactions for the release of friends and/or
family that have been charged by the authorities and to provide customers the ability to
cash a check without a bank account, was approved through RESOLUTION NO.
PC-2017-005 on February 8, 2018.

Pursuant to Palmdale Municipal Code Section 17.22.060, the Planning Commission may
review any Conditional Use Permit (CUP) to ensure that it is being operated in a manner
consistent with the conditions of approval or in a manner that is not detrimental to the
public health, safety, or welfare, or materially injurious to properties in the vicinity. After
review, if the Commission deems that there is sufficient evidence to warrant a full
investigation of CUP 17-016, a public hearing date to review the entitlement will be set.

Please provide direction to staff regarding initiation of a full investigation of the CUP,
which could include modifications to conditions of approval or revocation.
